transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-11-18
- Start: 14:00 PST
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Reddy (Redwood SE), Marta Silva (Velora Head of ML), Evan Brooks (Velora Platform Eng), Sofia Ortega (Velora Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Runbook rehearsal went through main steps, canary sizes discussed (1% then 10%), metrics for AB test (latency + quality) to be finalized, security asks around KMS and audit logs clarified.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, I think we have 55 minutes on the calendar so we'll run full runbook dry run and then spend the last 15 on AB gating decisions. Uh, quick check — any agenda items to add?
[00:12] Marta: No, that works. I want to make sure we validate the quality metric, like how do we detect a regression quickly.
[00:18] Jordan: Yep, that's on the list. Priya, you wanna kick off with the runbook walkthrough?
[00:22] Priya: Sure. So step one is pre-cutover smoke checks: model pinned to v1.3, health endpoints, and a prefix cache warmup. Note, we saw cache misses last week because the K V cash — the kv cache — had a TTL mismatch in staging. We patched that, and the patch is in the branch 'cache-fix-112'.
[00:38] Evan: Quick q, when you say prefix warmup, are you using our synthetic prompt set or production-like seed? Because last dry-run we used too-synthetic and it missed tail latencies.
[00:46] Priya: Good call. We'll use the production seed subset this time (the one Marta uploaded). Also we'll stagger the warmup so it doesn't spike token ingestion.
[00:55] Marta: Can we confirm what metric we call a regression? We were thinking about a combined signal: 1) 95th p50? sorry, 95th latency, 2) quality delta > 3% in top-k rerank metric, and 3) reject rate increase.
[01:10] Jordan: That maps well to Redwood defaults, we can expose those as part of the AB gating. Priya, can Redwood's telemetry produce an immediate 'abort' flag if two out of three are breached in a 5-minute window?
[01:21] Priya: We have an alerting rule runner in the console; we can wire a runbook step that triggers automatic rollback if the rule flips. There's a small caveat: metric collection lag is about 30–45s in our hosted pipeline — so the abort action should be conservative by default.
[01:34] Sofia: From security, we need confirmation that any logs sent to your hosted telemetry are PII-free and that we can route only aggregated metrics to third party. Also KMS keys must be customer-managed for this workload.
[01:45] Jordan: Agreed, for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM and token redaction. Sofia, can you share the exact KMS policy we need?
[01:51] Sofia: I'll share it after the call; I'll also attach the SOC2 appendix for key rotation.
[02:00] Priya: Ok moving on, step two is canary choreography. Proposal: run two staged canaries — dry-run in staging (10–15 min), then a 1% production canary for 30 min, then 10% for 1 hour if all green. The rollback criteria we just discussed would apply at each step.
[02:20] Marta: The 1% seems fine but our churn rate for clinical queries is sensitive, if we see a small shift in length or hallucination we need to abort fast. Can we set a stricter quality threshold for the initial 1%?
[02:34] Priya: Yes, we can set a different threshold for the 1% window — like quality delta > 2% triggers immediate rollback. Also keep latency SLO tighter for the initial canary.
[02:45] Evan: What instrumentation do we have inside the model path? We need traces for KV cache hits/misses and end-to-end token timing. Last time the trace ids weren't propagated.
[02:55] Priya: We added a trace-id pass-through to the front-end agent; Priya (sic) sorry, I mean, the change is in 'trace-pass-2025'. We'll share the trace extraction docs. There might be some transcription glitch here.
[03:12] Jordan: (laughs) classic transcription note. Priya will share that doc.
[03:18] Marta: For AB tests: we need to decide traffic split and the metric for the winner. Are we doing 50/50 for an AB over 24 hours or a staged ramp?
[03:28] Priya: Given production sensitivity, suggested is a staged AB: 20/20/60 for A/B/holdback? Sorry, that phrasing is confusing. More concretely: start 20% A, 20% B, 60% control for 6 hours, evaluate; then either shift to 50/50 or promote the winner. This avoids a sudden full cutover.
[03:45] Marta: We want the winner to be determined by quality-first criteria, then latency as tiebreaker.
[03:50] Jordan: Noted. We'll codify that in the runbook decision table.
[03:54] Sofia: A few security clarifications: audit logs need to be immutable for 90 days, and we need an access matrix for who can perform the rollback. Can Redwood enforce role-based controls that only our SREs + Redwood AE can trigger a rollback?
[04:07] Priya: We support RBAC and we can add a step that requires a two-person approval for production abort if you want. However automatic abort by metric can be set to run without approval. So choice there.
[04:20] Evan: Two-person manual abort is fine, but for automatic abort we want the noise floor low so we don't flip for spurious spikes. Suggest we require sliding window breach and minimum absolute delta.
[04:32] Jordan: Great feedback. We'll include exact thresholds in the draft.
[04:37] Jordan: Let's run a quick dry rehearsal: Priya, read step-by-step and we'll call out gaps.
[04:42] Priya: Step 0: Preflight checks (infra reachable, certs, routes). Step 1: Warmup prefixes with production seed. Step 2: Start staging dry-run for 15 minutes. Step 3: Run synthetic fallbacks and check redirect rules. Step 4: Create production 1% canary route, monitor metrics for 30 minutes. Step 5: Conditional roll to 10% for 1 hour. Step 6: If all green, schedule AB. Step 7: Post-cutover telemetry retention and rollback window close.
[05:08] Marta: On Step 3 — synthetic fallbacks — we need to whitelist our test account so the model doesn't redact important clinical phrases. Last time redaction policies stripped tokens and skewed evals.
[05:19] Priya: We'll use test account id 'velora-poc-test' and disable aggressive redaction for that account. We'll note that in the runbook.
[05:26] Evan: Network note: when you switch routes, will session affinity persist? We have long-lived streams for some clients.
[05:32] Priya: Session affinity is maintained via sticky token routing for up to 10 minutes; beyond that it's a new session. We'll document expected behaviors.
[05:40] Jordan: Ok, pause. Any blockers remaining to run the dry-canary this week?
[05:45] Marta: For me, only the AB metric threshold to be defined.
[05:48] Evan: VPC peering verification pending, I can wrap that up by tomorrow morning.
[05:52] Sofia: KMS policy and audit appendix will be in your inbox by EOD tomorrow.
[06:00] Jordan: Cool. Priya, two staged dry-run tasks — can you commit to performing them and sharing telemetry?
[06:05] Priya: Yes, I'll run two dry runs, one with 1% production seed and one with 10% synthetic and upload trace logs to the shared folder.
[06:12] Marta: On AB success criteria — enumerating again: 1) Quality delta <= 2% for initial 1% canary, <=3% for longer windows; 2) 95th latency not increased more than 150ms; 3) Reject rate stable within 0.5%. If any breaches, abort.
[06:34] Jordan: We'll translate those into exact numeric alert rules.
[06:38] Priya: Quick operational note: our telemetry agent batches events and there's a 30–60s ingestion latency; for abort rules we'll use a short sliding window but account for lag. Also mention that traces may drop at very high QPS, so we'll capture a representative sample.
[06:56] Evan: Can you also share the temp credentials for the canary so our SRE can monitor in real time?
[07:02] Jordan: We'll provision a read-only dashboard for your SREs and a separate admin token for aborts.
[07:10] Sofia: Also need proof that logs don't contain PHI. Can Redwood provide a sample sanitized log?
[07:16] Priya: We can generate a sanitized example and share.
[07:22] Jordan: Okay moving toward wrap. Let's capture decisions: 1) Dry-run in staging this week, 2) Production 1% then 10% with thresholds Marta defined, 3) Two-person manual abort optional, automatic abort available with sliding window, 4) RBAC + KMS details to be shared by Sofia, 5) Jordan to send runbook doc with explicit decision table.
[07:44] Marta: One last question, do we want to run an A/B for model variants or a config toggle? The difference is telemetry complexity.
[07:54] Priya: A/B at routing-layer is easiest for variant comparison; config toggles require in-place model switches and longer warmup. So recommend routing AB.
[08:05] Marta: Routing AB then.
[08:10] Jordan: Great. We'll take action items and follow up. Thanks everyone.
[08:14] Meeting end.
